questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a combination of being able to next and with new friends from around the world and see an other study culture. I wanted to get out of my comfortzone and see how it was to study at an other university too.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Socially it have been a great experience, I have made friends for life. I relation to study environment it has been a very poor experience. We got all very stressed in the German system, everything we had to learn by heart and the professors was not always interested in our learning outcome. I felt like not seen and like a number. We was told the first day that we should not expect good teaching, because the professors rather wanted to work with their research. Only one course took there time to give some feedback on our work. The supervision for master student is not very good - I felt like ekstra work and not so welcome. One teacher even said "you can evaluate the course and I know what you will say, but I won't do anything about".

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it could improve, especially the German webside for Göttingen university

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a first meeting with all the officials which was good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There could have been more activities and maybe also activities with German master students so we got a broader network.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A student dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It really depends on your flatmates and where you get a student dorm how it will turn out. I lived a very poor place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was complicated and took a long time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to send papers we had scanned and it was a bit difficult to find the right person to send the papers to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was the student office and that helped

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was pretty straight forward

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time and talk to your fellow students and if you are lucky getting some knowledge that are useful for the others, spread the word!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses from first year and second year were overlapping

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: IT found the level low in some course and very high in one specific course. IT was forest monitoring. It was very hard because it was taught old school, with learning even formulars by hard for the exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very old school and there is not much discussion for getting deeper in the topics.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Monitoring of Forest Resources, Forest Management under Different Climatic Conditions, Bioclimatology and Global Change, Research Planning, Ecological Functions of Wildlife: Implications for Conservation and Management.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bioclimatology and Global Change

questions.answer: Food were cheaper than DK, but transportation was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of courses and sports activites. Very nice!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend bouldering and Salsa dance. It was here I got away form all the academic pressure.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and explore Germany by train or hitch hiking. I have been great for me. There is a lot to see!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright because im a dane in Germany, but people seemed to be very closed and stressed most for the time. So it was a bit harder than expected

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is a good idea to good for a course in something you like, there you will get to know somebody and make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The distance to professors and authorities in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I don't really know. None.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would not recommend any to go here. I would tell them that it is not very pleasant to be a student here. Be prepared for a lot of struggle with the system and you have to try hard to get friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned how to handle ekstrem pressure and living under uncertain conditions.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it was dealing with all the worlds problems and my thoughts about them, when you had to focus and study at the same time being under a let of unnecessary pressure .

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
